chunks: From him, from Ibrahim ibn Ishaq, from al-Husayn ibn Abi al-Sarri, from al-Hasan ibn Ibrahim, from Yazid ibn Harun al-Wasiti, who said:

I asked Ja'far ibn Muhammad (peace be upon him) about the farmers, and he said: 'They are the sowers, the treasures of God in His land. And among all deeds, there is nothing more beloved to God than agriculture. And God did not send a Prophet except that he was a sower, except Idris (peace be upon him), for indeed he was a tailor.'
ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual status of farmers and agriculture in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam Ja'far al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) elevates agriculture to a sacred profession, describing farmers as 'God's treasures in His land' and asserting that cultivation is among the most beloved deeds to Him. He establishes a strong prophetic precedent by noting that all Prophets were farmers, with the sole exception of Idris (peace be upon him), who was a tailor, thereby validating agricultural labor as a fundamental aspect of divine service and human sustenance.
